diagnostics.message:
[final-glm-5.3-flash-effort-high-run1]
:resource.helm_release.elk installs the ELK stack whose Elasticsearch, Kibana, Filebeat, APM and Metricbeat pods all pull username/password from the `elastic-credentials` Secret (extraEnvs secretKeyRef). That Secret is created by :resource.kubernetes_secret.elasticsearch_credentials, but the release has no dependency on it — on a fresh apply the pods will fail to start (CreateContainerConfigError) if the Secret isn't applied first. No attribute reference or depends_on expresses this ordering.

----------------------------------------

[final-glm-5.3-flash-effort-high-run2]
helm_release.elk deploys Elasticsearch configured with secretKeyRefs to secret "elastic-credentials" (extraEnvs ELASTIC_PASSWORD/ELASTIC_USERNAME), but has no dependency on kubernetes_secret.elasticsearch_credentials, so pods can be scheduled before the secret exists.

----------------------------------------

[final-glm-5.3-flash-effort-high-run3]
:resource.helm_release.elk references the secret "elastic-credentials" by name in its values (ELASTIC_PASSWORD / ELASTIC_USERNAME env vars via secretKeyRef), but has no dependency on :resource.kubernetes_secret.elasticsearch_credentials. On a fresh apply the helm release can be installed before the secret exists, causing Elasticsearch pods to fail with CreateContainerConfigError. Add an explicit depends_on for this secret.

[final-glm-5.3-flash-effort-high-run1]
:resource.helm_release.elk mounts the `elastic-certificates` Secret (TLS key/cert) via secretMounts into Elasticsearch, Kibana, Filebeat, APM and Metricbeat containers. That Secret is created by :resource.kubernetes_secret.elasticsearch_certificates, but the release has no dependency on it, so pods can come up before the certificates exist. This ordering is not captured by any attribute reference or depends_on.

----------------------------------------

[final-glm-5.3-flash-effort-high-run2]
helm_release.elk mounts secret "elastic-certificates" into Elasticsearch, Kibana, Filebeat and APM pods (secretMounts / TLS config), but has no dependency on kubernetes_secret.elasticsearch_certificates.

----------------------------------------

[final-glm-5.3-flash-effort-high-run3]
:resource.helm_release.elk mounts the secret "elastic-certificates" (secretMounts for TLS certs) referenced by name in its values, but has no dependency on :resource.kubernetes_secret.elasticsearch_certificates. Without ordering, Elasticsearch/Kibana/filebeat pods can start before the TLS certificates secret exists and crash. Add an explicit depends_on for this secret.

[final-glm-5.3-flash-effort-high-run1]
:resource.helm_release.elk's Elasticsearch keystore reads the `elasticsearch-s3-user-creds` Secret (S3 snapshot credentials) via secretName in the keystore values. That Secret is created by :resource.kubernetes_secret.elasticsearch_s3_user_creds, but the release has no dependency on it; if the keystore secret is missing when Elasticsearch initializes, snapshot repository setup breaks. No attribute reference or depends_on establishes this ordering.

----------------------------------------

[final-glm-5.3-flash-effort-high-run2]
helm_release.elk configures the Elasticsearch keystore from secret "elasticsearch-s3-user-creds" (S3 snapshot repository credentials), but has no dependency on kubernetes_secret.elasticsearch_s3_user_creds.

----------------------------------------

[final-glm-5.3-flash-effort-high-run3]
:resource.helm_release.elk mounts the secret "elasticsearch-s3-user-creds" into the keystore (S3 snapshot repository credentials) referenced by name in its values, but has no dependency on :resource.kubernetes_secret.elasticsearch_s3_user_creds. On a fresh apply the S3 snapshot user credentials may not be in place when the release is installed, breaking snapshot/keystore setup. Add an explicit depends_on for this secret.

[final-glm-5.3-flash-effort-high-run1]
:resource.helm_release.elk's Kibana deployment reads the `kibana-encryption-key` Secret (KIBANA_ENCRYPTION_KEY) via secretKeyRef. That Secret is created by :resource.kubernetes_secret.kibana_enc_key, but the release has no dependency on it, so on a fresh apply Kibana can start before the encryption key exists and crash. This ordering is not expressed by any attribute reference or depends_on.

----------------------------------------

[final-glm-5.3-flash-effort-high-run2]
helm_release.elk deploys Kibana which reads KIBANA_ENCRYPTION_KEY from secret "kibana-encryption-key", but the release has no dependency on kubernetes_secret.kibana_enc_key.

----------------------------------------

[final-glm-5.3-flash-effort-high-run3]
:resource.helm_release.elk references the secret "kibana-encryption-key" via secretKeyRef (KIBANA_ENCRYPTION_KEY) in its kibana values, but has no dependency on :resource.kubernetes_secret.kibana_enc_key. Without ordering, the Kibana pod can start before the secret exists and fail. Add an explicit depends_on for this secret.
